mainTopic: תודוס's whole roasted goat and whose view the ברייתא follows; the custom of lighting a lamp on the night of יום הכפורים; the ברכה over fire only on מוצאי שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing the ברייתא about תודוס of Rome, who served a whole roasted goat (גדי מקולס) on פסח night. That looked close to eating קדשים outside the מקדש. The גמרא explains the rule: a whole roasted goat is a problem even in silence, while ordinary meat is a problem only if one says 'for פסח.' It then asks whether the ברייתא can follow רבי שמעון, who says an unusual pledge means nothing. It concludes that the ברייתא fits רבי יוסי, because רבי יוסי does not accept רבי שמעון's extra rule. Next it asks whether תודוס was a great scholar or a strongman. His Torah teaching about חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה learning from the frogs shows his greatness, and רבי יוסי בר אבין adds that he supported תלמידי חכמים. A new משנה follows: lighting a lamp at home on the night of יום הכפורים depends on local custom, and the גמרא says both customs aim to keep people from sin. The amud ends with the rule that the ברכה over fire is said only on מוצאי שבת, and a story showing how רבה בר בר חנה drew this rule out of רבי יוחנן's words. רב יוסף's verse about this story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: close to feeding Jews sacred meat outside
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the ברייתא about תודוס give the reason for the objection. Serving a whole roasted goat on פסח night looks almost like eating קדשים outside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: [You are] close to feeding the Jewish people sacred meat outside [the permitted area].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the ברייתא about תודוס. These words give the reason the חכמים objected to his practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole roasted goat on פסח night looks exactly like a קרבן פסח. Since there is no מקדש, people might think he is eating real קדשים outside, which is forbidden. The word 'close' (קרוב) shows it is not actual קדשים, only something that looks like it.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside (the place where קדשים may be eaten)

steps.confusionAlert: The meat is NOT actually קדשים. The problem is only that it looks like קדשים, so people may get the wrong idea.

phrases.english: [You are] close to feeding the Jewish people
phrases.notes: Part of the message the חכמים sent to תודוס

phrases.english: consecrated meat outside [the permitted area].
phrases.notes: Eating קדשים outside their proper place is forbidden

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרוֹב לְהַאֲכִיל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל קָדָשִׁים בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun on the previous section of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Serving a whole roasted goat on פסח night is close to feeding Jews קדשים outside the מקדש, so the practice is objectionable.

steps.title: Inference from the ברייתא: only a whole roasted goat is a problem
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא objects only to a whole roasted goat. That suggests meat not roasted whole is fine, which seems to contradict רב's broader ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: Roasted whole — yes [it is forbidden]; not roasted whole — no [it is not forbidden]!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a hidden meaning into the ברייתא. Since it only objected to a goat roasted whole, regular meat should be allowed, and that contradicts רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב forbade even saying 'this meat is for פסח,' with no mention of roasting it whole. The ברייתא seems to forbid only the whole roasted goat. So the ברייתא appears more lenient than רב, and the גמרא raises this as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Roasted whole, with its legs and innards (like the קרבן פסח)

phrases.english: Roasted whole — yes [it is forbidden],
phrases.notes: What the ברייתא explicitly objects to

phrases.english: not roasted whole — no [it is not forbidden]!
phrases.notes: The inference, which clashes with רב

steps.triggerLanguage: מְקוּלָּס — אִין, שֶׁאֵין מְקוּלָּס — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא just quoted and sets it against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that it is forbidden to say 'this meat is for פסח' (without requiring a whole roasted animal)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits the objection to a whole roasted goat. That implies other meat is fine, which contradicts רב's broader ban.

steps.title: Answer: whole roast is always a problem, other meat only if he says 'for פסח'
steps.stepSummary: The answer explains when each kind of meat is a problem. A whole roasted goat is a problem whether or not he says anything. Meat not roasted whole is a problem only if he says out loud that it is for פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: roasted whole — it makes no difference whether he said [it is for פסח] or did not say. Not roasted whole — if he specified, yes [forbidden]; if he did not specify, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. It shows that the ברייתא and רב are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole roasted goat looks like a קרבן פסח on its own, so it is forbidden even in silence. Regular meat looks like a קרבן only when he declares 'for פסח,' and that is the case רב was talking about. The ברייתא's inference ('not roasted whole is allowed') applies only when he says nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to create the problem. (1) Roasting a goat whole is forbidden even in silence. (2) Saying 'this meat is for פסח' is forbidden even for regular meat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical custom of not eating a whole roasted animal on the סדר night. It is also why we avoid calling meat 'for פסח.'

phrases.english: They say: [a goat] roasted whole —
phrases.notes: First case

phrases.english: it makes no difference if he said [it is for פסח],
and no difference if he did not say.
phrases.notes: Either way it is forbidden

phrases.english: Not roasted whole:
phrases.notes: Second case

phrases.english: if he specified [for פסח] — yes, forbidden;
phrases.notes: This is רב's case

phrases.english: if he did not specify — no, not forbidden.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's inference

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי, מְקוּלָּס: לָא שְׁנָא אֲמַר, לָא שְׁנָא לָא אֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (אוקימתא of each source to a different scenario)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows any meat not roasted whole, contradicting רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא allows non-whole meat only when nothing is said. רב forbids it when one declares 'for פסח.'

steps.title: רב אחא teaches the ברייתא in the name of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא had a different version of the ברייתא about תודוס. In his version, it was taught according to רבי שמעון, not רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא teaches this ברייתא according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of who said the ברייתא. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the version quoted earlier, the ברייתא was said by רבי יוסי. רב אחא attributes it to רבי שמעון instead. The גמרא will now test whether רבי שמעון could really hold this view.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching (here referring to the ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: Here מתניתין does not mean 'our משנה.' It refers to the ברייתא about תודוס.

phrases.english: Rav Acha teaches it —
this teaching — according to Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: Instead of רבי יוסי

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא מַתְנִי לַהּ לְהָא מַתְנִיתִין כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the content of the ברייתא to the question of who said it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב אחא's version, the ברייתא about תודוס is attributed to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב ששת: רבי שמעון holds an improper pledge means nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת objects to רב אחא's version. רבי שמעון exempts someone who pledges a barley מנחה, because that is not how people donate. By the same logic, saying 'this meat is for פסח' should mean nothing, so there should be no concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: It works for the one who teaches it according to רבי יוסי. But does it work for the one who teaches it according to רבי שמעון? Didn't we learn in a משנה: רבי שמעון exempts him, because he did not donate in the way donors donate?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges רב אחא's version. He argues that רבי שמעון could not be worried about meat that only looks like קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, someone pledges a barley מנחה, but a מנחה must be wheat. רבי שמעון says the pledge means nothing because it is not a normal way to donate. Likewise, one cannot consecrate already-slaughtered meat as a קרבן פסח. So according to רבי שמעון, saying 'this meat is for פסח' should be meaningless, with no reason to worry.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?
In the normal way people donate

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet strongly objected to it:
Granted, according to the one who learns it
according to Rabbi Yosei — it works well,
but according to the one who teaches it
according to Rabbi Shimon — does it work well?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical; the answer is no

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: Rabbi Shimon exempts [him],
phrases.notes: Refers to one who pledged a barley מנחה

phrases.english: because he did not donate in the manner of donors.
phrases.notes: An improper pledge has no effect

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּתָנֵי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אחא's attribution from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא's attribution of the ברייתא to רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון ignores pledges not made in the normal way of donors. Saying 'this meat is for פסח' is not a normal consecration, so it should have no effect and cause no concern.

steps.title: רבינא: the same problem exists for רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether the version with רבי יוסי really works any better. רבא said רבי שמעון's view follows רבי יוסי, who holds a person is held to the end of his words too. So רבי יוסי should also say 'meat… for פסח' cancels itself out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: And does it work for the one who teaches it according to רבי יוסי? Didn't רבא say: רבי שמעון said his ruling following the approach of רבי יוסי, who said that a person is held even to the end of his words?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא turns רב ששת's challenge around. He shows that the 'easy' version with רבי יוסי has the same problem. His challenge continues in the next step, and step 8 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא explained that רבי שמעון cancels the barley מנחה only because he follows רבי יוסי's rule that the end of a statement also counts. The word 'barley' undoes the word 'מנחה.' If that rule comes from רבי יוסי, then for him too, 'meat' should undo 'for פסח,' leaving no reason to worry.

keyTerms.meaning: Is held to / is bound by

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב ששת's challenge with רבינא's. רב ששת said only the רבי שמעון version is hard. רבינא shows that the רבי יוסי version is equally hard, because רבי שמעון's logic comes from רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
And the one who teaches it according to Rabbi Yosei —
does it work well?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical challenge

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said it following the approach of Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: Regarding the barley מנחה

phrases.english: who said: even by the end of his words
a person is held.
phrases.notes: So 'barley' undoes 'מנחה,' and 'meat' should undo 'for פסח'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וּמַאן דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מִי נִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב ששת's challenge so that it hits the רבי יוסי version too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption from step 5 that the ברייתא fits well with רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא said רבי שמעון's ruling rests on רבי יוסי's principle that the end of a statement counts. So רבי יוסי should also treat 'meat for פסח' as self-cancelling, leaving no concern about קדשים.

steps.title: Does the agreement work both ways?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא finishes his challenge. Since רבי שמעון agrees with רבי יוסי, maybe רבי יוסי also agrees with רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, is it not so? Since רבי שמעון holds like רבי יוסי, רבי יוסי also holds like רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from Step 6. It suggests that the two תנאים fully agree, so moving the ברייתא to רבי יוסי would not help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said רבי שמעון's view is built on רבי יוסי's view. רבינא assumes this means the two hold exactly the same. If so, רבי יוסי would also say 'this meat is for פסח' means nothing, and רב ששת's question comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What, is it not…?' — introduces a suggested conclusion
holds like, agrees with the view of

phrases.english: What, is it not so?

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Since Rabbi Shimon holds like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי נָמֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן!
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei also holds like Rabbi Shimon!
phrases.notes: So the problem with רבי שמעון would apply to רבי יוסי too.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו: מִדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבינא's challenge begun in Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The version of the ברייתא that follows רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון hold the same view, then רב ששת's objection against רבי שמעון also works against רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The agreement goes only one way
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון builds on רבי יוסי, but רבי יוסי does not accept רבי שמעון's extra rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. רבי שמעון holds like רבי יוסי, but רבי יוסי does not hold like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבינא's suggestion. The agreement is one-directional, so the version with רבי יוסי still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון accepts רבי יוסי's idea that a person's last words count too. But רבי שמעון adds his own rule: an unusual pledge, one people don't normally make, means nothing at all. רבי יוסי never accepts that extra rule. So for רבי יוסי, the words 'for פסח' are not cancelled by the word 'meat.' The declaration still carries some weight, so there is still a reason to worry about it looking like קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: No — introduces a rejection of the suggestion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'A holds like B' always means 'B holds like A.' Here רבי שמעון uses רבי יוסי's idea as a base and then adds more. רבי יוסי does not take on that addition.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about תודוס works best according to רבי יוסי. He counts a person's last words but does not erase the first words. רבי שמעון also says an unusual pledge means nothing.

phrases.english: No,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon holds like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: but Rabbi Yosei does not hold like Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון hold exactly the same view, so both would say the words 'meat… for פסח' mean nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי שמעון says an unusual pledge means nothing. For רבי יוסי the words still count, so the ברייתא fits him.

steps.title: Was תודוס a great scholar or a strongman?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: did the חכמים hold back from punishing תודוס because of his Torah, or because of his power?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was asked of them: Was תודוס איש רומי a great man, or was he a powerful strongman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the person in the ברייתא. The חכמים said they would have put him in נידוי, but they did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is why the חכמים held back. Was it out of respect for his Torah greatness? Or was it because he was powerful and dangerous, so they could not act?

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was asked of them' — introduces an open question
a great man, a Torah scholar
'a man of fists,' a powerful, forceful person

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
Todos of Rome —
was he a great man (a scholar),
or was he a powerful strongman?
phrases.notes: In that case they held back because they feared him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: תּוֹדוֹס אִישׁ רוֹמִי גַּבְרָא רַבָּה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the person in the ברייתא discussed earlier
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים did not put תודוס in נידוי: because of his Torah greatness or because of his power

steps.title: A teaching of תודוס about the fiery furnace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a Torah teaching from תודוס. It asks why חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה let themselves be thrown into the furnace.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: This too תודוס איש רומי taught: What did חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה see that made them give themselves over to the fiery furnace for קדושת השם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof from a Torah teaching of תודוס himself. This step only sets up his question; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the fact that תודוס taught Torah publicly. That suggests he was a scholar. His question asks what source חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה used to choose death over bowing to the idol.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear' — introduces a source as proof

phrases.english: Come and hear.

phrases.aramaic: עוֹד זוֹ דָּרַשׁ תּוֹדוֹס אִישׁ רוֹמִי:
phrases.english: This too Todos of Rome expounded:
What did Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya see
that they gave [themselves] over for sanctifying God's name
to the fiery furnace?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע. עוֹד זוֹ דָּרַשׁ תּוֹדוֹס אִישׁ רוֹמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question of Step 9
steps.raayaObject: That תודוס was a גברא רבה, a Torah scholar
steps.raayaSupportSource: A public Torah teaching (דרשה) given by תודוס

steps.title: The קל וחומר from the frogs
steps.stepSummary: The frogs went into hot ovens even without a מצוה of קדושת השם. Jews, who have that מצוה, should surely do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: They made a קל וחומר from the frogs. Frogs are not commanded about קדושת השם, yet it says about them: 'They will come up into your house… and into your ovens and your kneading bowls.' When are kneading bowls near the oven? When the oven is hot. We, who are commanded about קדושת השם, must do so all the more.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the content of תודוס's teaching, a clever Torah derivation. It finishes the proof that he was a real Torah scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dough is kneaded near the oven while the oven is hot and ready for baking. So the frogs jumped into burning ovens to fulfill God's command. If frogs were willing to do that, people who are actually commanded about קדושת השם must surely be willing too. A sharp teaching like this shows תודוס was a גברא רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lesser case to a greater one

steps.whatToRemember: תודוס taught a sharp Torah lesson in public: the frogs entered hot ovens, so we must surely give our lives for קדושת השם. This points to the conclusion that he was a גברא רבה, a Torah scholar, and not just a strongman.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is a well-known source showing that חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה derived מסירות נפש for קדושת השם by their own reasoning.

phrases.english: They made a kal vachomer for themselves from the frogs.
If frogs,
which are not commanded about sanctifying God's name,
it is written about them: 'And they will come [and go up] into your house [etc.]'
'and into your ovens and your kneading bowls,'
phrases.notes: שמות ז:כח

phrases.english: When are kneading bowls found near the oven?
You must say: when the oven is hot.
We, who are commanded about sanctifying God's name —
all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשְׂאוּ קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּעַצְמָן מִצְּפַרְדְּעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of תודוס's teaching introduced in Step 10
steps.raayaObject: That תודוס was a גברא רבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: His derivation of a קל וחומר from the frogs in שמות ז:כח

steps.title: תודוס Supported Torah Scholars with Money
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין gives another reason the חכמים honored תודוס: he invested money in businesses for תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: תודוס was someone who put merchandise into the pockets of תלמידי חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to the question of why the חכמים held back from punishing תודוס. It was not only his Torah or his power. It was that he supported Torah scholars with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 offered two options: his Torah or his power. Steps 10-11 showed that he had Torah. רבי יוסי בר אבין adds a new reason: he gave scholars business money so they could earn a living, and that earned him special respect.

keyTerms.meaning: Puts merchandise in, meaning he gives money so someone can run a business

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
one who casts merchandise into the purse
phrases.notes: He funded their businesses, often as a partner.

phrases.english: of Torah scholars, he was.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason for the honor shown to תודוס, beyond the Torah proven in steps 10-11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים held back from punishing תודוס.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because he financially supported תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: Supporting Scholars Earns a Seat in Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that whoever supports תלמידי חכמים sits in the heavenly yeshiva. The source is a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: anyone who puts merchandise into the pockets of Torah scholars merits to sit in the heavenly yeshiva. As it says: 'For in the shadow of wisdom is the shadow of money.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי יוסי בר אבין by showing how great it is to support Torah scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links wisdom and money as sharing one 'shade.' A person who gives the money gets to sit together with the people of wisdom. This explains why תודוס deserved such respect.

keyTerms.meaning: In the shadow of wisdom, in the shadow of money (קהלת ז:יב)

steps.whatToRemember: The story of תודוס ends with this lesson: supporting Torah scholars brings a reward close to that of learning itself.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמֵּטִיל מְלַאי לְכִיס תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
phrases.english: anyone who casts merchandise into the purse of Torah scholars
merits and sits in the heavenly academy,
as it is stated:
"For in the shadow of wisdom is the shadow of money."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 12 with a teaching and a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That supporting scholars is worthy of great honor.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן, based on קהלת ז:יב.

steps.title: משנה: Lighting a Lamp on יום הכפורים Night
steps.stepSummary: Whether people light a lamp at home on the night of יום הכפורים depends on local custom. Lamps are always lit in shuls, study halls, dark alleys, and near sick people.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a place where people are used to lighting a lamp on the night of יום הכפורים, they light. In a place where people are used to not lighting, they do not light. But everyone lights in shuls, study halls, dark alleys, and near sick people.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is another case of 'follow the local custom,' this time about a home lamp on the night of יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At home, the custom can go either way. The public and special places listed get light no matter what: shuls and study halls out of honor, dark alleys so no one gets hurt, and sick people because they need it.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where people have the custom

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is not about candles honoring the holiday the way שבת candles are. It is about whether to have light in the home on that night. The גמרא will explain why.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A place where they were accustomed to kindle the lamp
on Yom Kippur nights, they kindle.

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַדְלִיק — אֵין מַדְלִיקִין.
phrases.english: A place where they were accustomed not to kindle, they do not kindle.
And they kindle in synagogues and in study halls
and in dark alleyways
and next to the sick.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לְהַדְלִיק אֶת הַנֵּר בְּלֵילֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It continues the chapter's theme of local customs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lighting at home on the night of יום הכפורים follows local custom. Shuls, study halls, dark alleys, and sick people always get light.

steps.title: Both Customs Aim for the Same Goal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that those who light and those who do not light both have the same purpose in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: whether they said to light or said not to light, both meant the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה. Opposite customs come from one shared goal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marital relations are forbidden on יום הכפורים. One group lights a lamp because people avoid intimacy when there is light. The other group keeps it dark so spouses do not see each other and become tempted. Both are trying to keep people away from sin.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was taught:
Whether they said to kindle
or they said not to kindle,
both intended one thing.
phrases.notes: The goal is to keep people away from forbidden marital relations on יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: בֵּין שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְהַדְלִיק וּבֵין שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַדְלִיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the two customs in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both customs share one goal: preventing sin on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: רבא Praises Israel for Their Shared Intent
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the פסוק 'Your people are all righteous' onto this case. Different customs, but everyone is aiming for the good.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהושע said that רבא taught: 'Your people are all righteous, they will inherit the land forever.' Whether they said to light or said not to light, they both meant only one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attaches a פסוק to the idea from the ברייתא, turning it into praise of the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explained the logic of the two customs. רבא adds a message: even when Jews do opposite things, all of them are trying to do the right thing. That is why the פסוק calls them all צדיקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught or expounded, usually a פסוק
Your people are all righteous (ישעיה ס:כא)

steps.whatToRemember: Different customs on the night of יום הכפורים are not a conflict. Everyone shares the same holy goal.

phrases.english: Rav Yehoshua said: Rava expounded
"Your people are all righteous,
they shall inherit the land forever, etc."
whether they said to kindle
or they said not to kindle,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵיהֶם לֹא נִתְכַּוְּונוּ אֶלָּא לְדָבָר אֶחָד.
phrases.english: both intended nothing but one thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the ברייתא's idea and connects it to a פסוק praising Israel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opposite customs both reflect righteous intent.

steps.title: The Blessing over Fire Is Only on מוצאי שבת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the ברכה over fire is said only on מוצאי שבת, because that is when fire was first created.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: we only say the ברכה over fire on מוצאי שבת, since that is when it was first created.
steps.whatsHappening: Having talked about lamps on יום הכפורים, the גמרא brings a related rule. The ברכה 'בורא מאורי האש' is said only on מוצאי שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire was first created on מוצאי שבת, when אדם הראשון made fire. So the ברכה belongs to that time. The point is that on מוצאי יום הכפורים, this reason does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not make a ברכה on fire

steps.confusionAlert: Some later sources rule that a ברכה on fire is made on מוצאי יום הכפורים too. That opinion is based on a different reason: fire that 'rested' because using it was forbidden. Here שמואל is giving only the 'first creation' reason.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One does not bless over fire
except at the conclusion of Shabbat,
since it is the beginning of its creation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל הָאוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related topic: fire and lamps connected to יום הכפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה on fire is only said on מוצאי שבת.

steps.title: An Elder Confirms This in the Name of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: An elder, possibly רבה בר בר חנה, says שמואל is right, and that רבי יוחנן said the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to him, and some say it was רבה בר בר חנה: that is correct, and so said רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone backs up שמואל's rule by reporting that רבי יוחנן agreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the rule has two great supporters: שמואל in בבל and רבי יוחנן in ארץ ישראל. That makes it stronger.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him,
and some say it was Rabba bar bar Chana:
Well said,
and so said Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: יִשַׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's rule with רבי יוחנן's agreement.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule about the ברכה on fire.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A report that רבי יוחנן said the same.

steps.title: עולא Rides a Donkey with Two Students Beside Him
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: עולא is riding a donkey, with רבי אבא on his right and רבה בר בר חנה on his left.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא was riding a donkey and going along. רבי אבא was walking on his right, and רבה בר בר חנה was walking on his left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting the scene for a story. It prepares the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scene tells us who was there. Both רבי אבא and רבה בר בר חנה heard teachings of רבי יוחנן. That matters for the discussion about what רבי יוחנן really said.

phrases.english: Ulla was riding a donkey and going along,
and walking along were
Rabbi Abba on his right
and Rabba bar bar Chana on his left.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא הֲוָה רְכִיב חֲמָרָא וְאָזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story about the same teaching of רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבי אבא Asks עולא What He Reported from רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks עולא whether he really said in רבי יוחנן's name that the ברכה on fire is only on מוצאי שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to עולא: Is it true that you said in the name of רבי יוחנן, 'We only make a ברכה on fire on מוצאי שבת, since that is when it was first created'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא checks with עולא whether he really reported this rule from רבי יוחנן. This question sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא is not yet challenging the rule. He wants to confirm the exact report. The way the answer goes, with רבה בר בר חנה standing right there, will be important in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it certain? Is it true?
In the name of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Ulla:
Is it true that you said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan
"One does not bless over fire
except at the conclusion of Shabbat,
since it is the beginning of its creation"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְעוּלָּא: וַדַּאי דְּאָמְרִיתוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Within the story, רבי אבא asks to confirm the report of רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether עולא truly reported this rule in רבי יוחנן's name.

steps.title: עולא looks at רבה בר בר חנה with displeasure
steps.stepSummary: עולא realizes the quote must have come from רבה בר בר חנה, and he turns to look at him with displeasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא turned around and looked at רבה בר בר חנה with displeasure.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues without words. עולא turns and gives רבה בר בר חנה a displeased look, which sets up רבה בר בר חנה's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא knew he had never said this in רבי יוחנן's name. So he concluded that רבה בר בר חנה, who had also come from ארץ ישראל, must have said it, and he suspected a misquote. The look takes the place of a spoken complaint.

phrases.english: Ulla turned around and looked at him
phrases.notes: עולא was riding between the two; רבה בר בר חנה was on his left.

phrases.english: at Rabba bar bar Chana with displeasure.
phrases.notes: A silent complaint: 'Did you put words in רבי יוחנן's mouth?'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר עוּלָּא, חֲזָא בֵּיהּ בְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה בִּישׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is עולא's nonverbal reaction to רבי אבא's question in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative step: עולא signals that the quote did not come from him and suspects רבה בר בר חנה of misquoting.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה explains what he really quoted
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה says he never quoted רבי יוחנן about the fire ברכה. He quoted a different exchange about lighting a lamp on יום הכפורים that falls on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'I did not say it about that. I said it about this: a תנא taught before רבי יוחנן that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that when יום הכפורים falls on שבת, even in a place where they said not to light, one lights in honor of שבת. And רבי יוחנן answered after him: but the חכמים forbid.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה defends himself. He explains that רבי יוחנן never said the fire rule explicitly. His 'and so said רבי יוחנן' was based on what רבי יוחנן said in a different exchange, about the lamp on יום הכפורים that falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some places had a custom not to light a lamp on the night of יום הכפורים. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that when יום הכפורים falls on שבת, everyone lights, because a lamp honors שבת. רבי יוחנן added that the חכמים disagree and forbid it. רבה בר בר חנה did not hear the fire rule from רבי יוחנן directly. He inferred it from this comment of רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: a reciter who memorized and taught ברייתות

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about lighting שבת candles before the holiday begins. It is about the local custom of lighting or not lighting a lamp in the house on the night of יום הכפורים.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא לָאו אַהָא אֲמַרִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: I did not say it about that,
phrases.notes: 'That' means the ברכה on fire being only on מוצאי שבת.

phrases.english: rather, I said it about this:
that a reciter taught before Rabbi Yochanan,
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbat,
even in a place where they said not to light,
phrases.notes: Refers to the local custom not to light a lamp on the night of יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: one lights in honor of Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: וְעָנֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בָּתְרֵיהּ: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִים.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan answered after him: and the Sages forbid.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן completes the ברייתא with the opposing view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא לָאו אַהָא אֲמַרִי, אֶלָּא אַהָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers עולא's silent complaint from step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Implicitly: did רבה בר בר חנה misquote רבי יוחנן?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. He did not hear the fire rule from רבי יוחנן outright. He derived it from רבי יוחנן's comment 'and the חכמים forbid' about the lamp on יום הכפורים that falls on שבת.

steps.title: עולא accepts the explanation
steps.stepSummary: עולא accepts that this is what רבי יוחנן actually said.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Let it be that one.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא accepts רבה בר בר חנה's account and tells רבי אבא that this is the real statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The confusion is cleared up. רבי יוחנן's explicit statement was about lighting a lamp on יום הכפורים that falls on שבת. עולא accepts that the fire rule can rightly be traced back to that statement.

keyTerms.meaning: let it be that one (that is the real statement)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן never said 'the fire ברכה is only on מוצאי שבת' in so many words. רבה בר בר חנה drew it out of רבי יוחנן's comment 'and the חכמים forbid,' about lighting a lamp on יום הכפורים that falls on שבת. עולא accepted this.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let it be that one.
phrases.notes: עולא is speaking to רבי אבא: accept this as רבי יוחנן's statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עָדָא תְּהֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This accepts the clarification from step 22 and answers רבי אבא's question from step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's explicit statement was 'and the חכמים forbid' on the lamp question. The fire-ברכה rule was inferred from it by רבה בר בר חנה, and עולא accepted it.

steps.title: רב יוסף applies a verse to the story
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reads a פסוק from משלי about the deep thoughts in a person's heart onto this episode.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף read this verse about it: 'Counsel in the heart of a man is like deep water...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף comments on the story by quoting a פסוק. The quote continues past the end of this passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse describes a person's hidden thoughts as deep water. It fits a story where much happened without words: עולא's silent look and רבה בר בר חנה understanding it. The second half of the verse, which completes the point, comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef read about it:
"Counsel in the heart of a man is like deep water;
phrases.notes: משלי כ:ה. The verse continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a closing comment on the whole donkey-ride episode.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Aggadic application: the silent exchange is like deep water in a person's heart.
